ClearingStatus.description:
Clearing status for OTC derivatives.

Determines whether a trade is cleared through a CCP or remains bilateral
under a CSA agreement.

oneOf.description:
Bilateral (uncleared) trade governed by CSA

Subject to BCBS-IOSCO margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives.
Requires both VM and IM (above thresholds).

Trade cleared through a central counterparty (CCP)

Margin requirements set by the CCP. IM is typically VaR-based.
VM is exchanged daily with no threshold.

CollateralAssetClass.description:
Collateral asset classes per BCBS-IOSCO standards.

Asset classes determine baseline haircuts and eligibility criteria.
The BCBS-IOSCO framework specifies minimum haircuts by asset class.

# Reference

BCBS-IOSCO "Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives" (2020)
Annex A: Standardized haircut schedule `docs/REFERENCES.md#bcbs-iosco-uncleared-margin`

oneOf.description: Cash in eligible currency
Sovereign government bonds accepted as collateral.
Debt issued or guaranteed by eligible agencies.
Covered bonds meeting the applicable eligibility criteria.
Investment-grade corporate bonds accepted under the CSA.
Eligible listed equity collateral.
Eligible gold collateral.
Eligible mutual funds or exchange-traded funds.

CollateralEligibility.description:
Single collateral eligibility entry.

Defines eligibility criteria and haircut for a specific type of collateral.

concentration_limit.description:
Concentration limit as fraction of total collateral (optional)

E.g., 0.30 means max 30% of collateral can be this type.

fx_haircut_addon.description:
Additional FX haircut for currency mismatch (decimal)

Applied when collateral currency differs from settlement currency.

min_rating.description:
Minimum credit rating requirement (e.g., "A-", "BBB")

If None, no rating constraint applies.

CsaSpec.description:
Credit Support Annex specification (ISDA standard).

The CSA governs the exchange of collateral between counterparties
for OTC derivatives. This specification captures all key commercial
terms needed for margin calculation and management.

# ISDA Documentation

This type represents terms from:
- ISDA 2016 Credit Support Annex for Variation Margin (VM CSA)
- ISDA 2018 Credit Support Annex for Initial Margin (IM CSA)

# References

- ISDA 2016 VM CSA: `docs/REFERENCES.md#isda-vm-csa-2016`
- ISDA 2018 IM CSA: `docs/REFERENCES.md#isda-im-csa-2018`
- BCBS-IOSCO uncleared margin framework: `docs/REFERENCES.md#bcbs-iosco-uncleared-margin`

# Example

```
use finstack_quant_margin::{
    CsaSpec, VmParameters, ImParameters, EligibleCollateralSchedule,
    MarginCallTiming, ImMethodology, MarginTenor,
};
use finstack_quant_core::currency::Currency;
use finstack_quant_core::money::Money;

# fn main() -> finstack_quant_core::Result<()> {
let csa = CsaSpec {
    id: "USD-CSA-2024".to_string(),
    base_currency: Currency::USD,
    vm_params: VmParameters::regulatory_standard(Currency::USD)?,
    im_params: Some(ImParameters::simm_standard(Currency::USD)?),
    eligible_collateral: EligibleCollateralSchedule::bcbs_standard()?,
    call_timing: MarginCallTiming::regulatory_standard()?,
    collateral_curve_id: "USD-OIS".into(),
    calendar_id: "usny".into(),
};
# Ok(())
# }
```

base_currency.description:
Base currency for margin calculations.

All exposures and collateral values are converted to this currency
for netting and comparison with thresholds.

calendar_id.description: Contractual business-day calendar for calls and settlements.

collateral_curve_id.description:
Discount curve ID for collateral valuation.

Cash collateral is typically discounted at OIS/RFR rates.
This curve should match the CSA's collateral interest rate.

eligible_collateral.description:
Eligible collateral schedule.

Defines what collateral types are acceptable and associated haircuts.

im_params.description:
Initial margin parameters (optional).

If None, no IM is exchanged (either not in scope for regulations
or trade is cleared).

vm_params.description:
Variation margin parameters.

Governs daily mark-to-market collateral exchange.

default_haircut.description:
Default haircut for unlisted collateral (if accepted)

If None, only explicitly listed collateral types are accepted.

eligible.description: List of eligible collateral types with haircuts

rehypothecation_allowed.description:
Whether rehypothecation of posted collateral is permitted

For IM under BCBS-IOSCO rules, rehypothecation is prohibited.
For VM, rehypothecation may be permitted by bilateral agreement.

attributes.description: Attributes for scenario selection and tagging

discrete_dividends.description:
Optional discrete cash dividends `(ex_date, amount)` for the underlying.

When non-empty, pricing uses explicit period dividend pass-through and does
not add continuous-yield dividend return to avoid double counting.

dividend_settlement.description: Settlement timing for explicit manufactured dividends.

dividend_tax_rate.description:
Dividend withholding tax rate for net return calculation.

Specifies the fraction of dividends withheld for tax (e.g., 0.15 for 15% withholding).
When set to 0.0 (default), the TRS passes through 100% of dividends (gross return).
When set to a positive value, the dividend return component is reduced:
```text
net_dividend_return = gross_dividend_return × (1 - dividend_tax_rate)
```

# Market Context

Withholding tax varies by jurisdiction and investor domicile:
- US qualified dividends: typically 0% for domestic investors
- US non-qualified: up to 30% for foreign investors (varies by treaty)
- European: varies by country (15-30% typical)

financing.description: Financing leg specification (curves, spread, day count).

initial_level.description:
Optional first-period start level.

Pricing uses this only when the first period is in progress and no
matching entry exists in `past_fixings`. Future periods use live spot.

instrument_pricing_overrides.description: Attributes for scenario selection and tagging.

margin_spec.description:
Optional OTC margin specification for VM/IM.

Equity TRS use SIMM equity bucket for margin calculation.

past_fixings.description:
Observed underlying levels at past reset (period-start) dates.

For a seasoned TRS valued inside a return period, the total-return leg
must anchor the current period to the level *observed* at the period
start so the realized spot move enters the PV (equity delta). Provide
`(reset_date, level)` pairs for every period-start date on or before
the valuation date; the first period may use `initial_level` instead.
Pricing errors when the current period's start level is unavailable.

underlying.description: Underlying equity parameters (spot ID, dividend yield, contract size).

EquityUnderlyingParams.description: Equity underlying parameters for options and equity-linked swaps.

spot_id.description: Spot price identifier in market data

compounding.description:
Rate-compounding convention (term-rate vs overnight-compounded).

Defaults to [`FinancingRateCompounding::TermRate`]. Set to
[`FinancingRateCompounding::OvernightCompounded`] for SOFR/SONIA/€STR
overnight-funded TRS so the financing rate captures daily-compounding
convexity.

day_count.description: Day count convention for accrual calculations

discount_curve_id.description: Discount curve identifier for present value calculations

spread_bp.description: Spread in basis points over the floating rate (e.g., 50 = 50bp = 0.5%)

FinancingRateCompounding.description:
Rate-compounding convention for a TRS financing leg.

Distinguishes how each accrual period's floating rate is projected from the
forward curve. The two conventions differ by the daily-compounding convexity
— typically 12–15 bp of rate at current levels on an upward-sloping curve.

oneOf.description:
Term-rate financing (e.g. 3M Term SOFR, EURIBOR): the period rate is the
simple arithmetic-average forward over the accrual period. This is the
default and matches a conventional term-rate-funded TRS.

Overnight-indexed (OIS / RFR) financing — SOFR, SONIA, €STR, TONA: the
period rate daily-compounds the overnight forward,
`R = (∏(1 + rᵢ·dᵢ) − 1) / τ`, picking up the compounding convexity that
the simple arithmetic average drops.

ImMethodology.description:
Initial margin calculation methodology.

Different methodologies are used depending on regulatory requirements,
product type, and whether trades are cleared or bilateral.

# BCBS-IOSCO Standards

For bilateral (uncleared) OTC derivatives, either SIMM or the regulatory
schedule approach may be used. SIMM is the industry standard for large
dealers due to its risk-sensitivity.

oneOf.description:
Haircut-based IM calculation (standard for repos and securities financing)

IM = Collateral_Value × Haircut

Haircuts are determined by asset class, rating, maturity, and FX mismatch.

ISDA Standard Initial Margin Model (SIMM)

Sensitivities-based model calculating IM from delta, vega, and curvature
risk across interest rate, credit, equity, commodity, and FX risk classes.

Reference: ISDA SIMM Methodology v2.6 (2023)

BCBS-IOSCO regulatory schedule approach

Grid-based IM calculation using notional × rate based on asset class and maturity.
Simpler but typically more conservative than SIMM.

Example rates:
- Interest Rate: 0-2yr: 1%, 2-5yr: 2%, 5+yr: 4%
- Credit: 2-5yr: 5%, 5+yr: 10%
- Equity: 15%
- FX: 6%

Internal model approved by regulator

Bank's proprietary VaR or ES-based model approved by supervisor.
Must meet regulatory backtesting and validation requirements.

Clearing house methodology

CCP-specific IM calculation (typically VaR or SPAN-based).
Examples: LCH SwapClear, CME, ICE Clear Credit

ImParameters.description:
Initial margin parameters.

Initial margin is collateral posted to cover potential future exposure (PFE)
during the close-out period following a default. IM is required for
non-centrally cleared derivatives under BCBS-IOSCO rules.

# Margin Period of Risk (MPOR)

The MPOR determines the horizon over which PFE is calculated:
- Standard: 10 business days for bilateral derivatives
- Reduced: 5 days for certain liquid products

# Example

```
use finstack_quant_margin::{ImMethodology, ImParameters};
use finstack_quant_core::currency::Currency;
use finstack_quant_core::money::Money;

let im_params = ImParameters {
    methodology: ImMethodology::Simm,
    mpor_days: 10,
    threshold: Money::from((50_000_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    mta: Money::from((0_i64, Currency::USD)), // Combined with VM MTA
    segregated: true,
};
```

methodology.description:
IM calculation methodology.

Options include SIMM, regulatory schedule, or CCP methodology.

mpor_days.description:
Margin Period of Risk in business days.

Standard is 10 days under BCBS-IOSCO. CCPs may use shorter periods.

mta.description:
Minimum Transfer Amount for IM.

Combined IM+VM MTA must not exceed €500,000 under BCBS-IOSCO.

segregated.description:
Whether IM must be held in a segregated account.

Under BCBS-IOSCO, IM must be segregated with a third-party custodian
to protect it in case of the collecting party's insolvency.

threshold.description:
IM threshold (aggregate group level).

BCBS-IOSCO permits €50M aggregate threshold at group level.
Many large dealers operate with zero threshold by agreement.

InstrumentSchema.description: Canonical schema marker for persisted instrument envelopes.

MarginCallTiming.description:
Margin call timing parameters.

Specifies the operational timing for margin calls including
notification and dispute resolution windows.

delivery_grace_days.description: Grace period for collateral delivery (business days)

notification_deadline_hours.description: Notification deadline (hours after valuation, e.g., 13:00 local time)

MarginTenor.description:
Margin call frequency.

Determines how often margin calls are made and collateral is exchanged.
Industry standard for OTC derivatives is daily under BCBS-IOSCO rules.

oneOf.description: Daily margin calls (standard for OTC derivatives post-2016)
Weekly margin calls (pre-regulatory period)
Monthly margin calls (pre-regulatory period)
On-demand margin calls (used for repos and some bilateral agreements)

MaturityConstraints.description:
Maturity constraints for eligible collateral.

Some CSAs restrict collateral based on remaining maturity to limit
duration risk in the collateral portfolio.

max_remaining_years.description: Maximum remaining years to maturity (if any)

min_remaining_years.description: Minimum remaining years to maturity (if any)

clearing_status.description: Clearing status: bilateral or cleared through CCP

csa.description:
Full CSA specification (for bilateral trades)

For cleared trades, this represents the terms with the CCP.

im_methodology.description:
Initial margin calculation methodology

- Bilateral: SIMM or Schedule
- Cleared: ClearingHouse (CCP-specific)

settlement_lag.description: Settlement lag for margin transfers (business days)

simm_credit_classification.description:
Explicit SIMM credit classification for credit-sensitive instruments.

Required when a credit product uses `ImMethodology::Simm`; leave `None`
for non-credit instruments and non-SIMM margin methodologies.

SimmCreditClassification.description:
Explicit ISDA SIMM credit risk-class and bucket assignment.

Corporate, sovereign, and index credit exposures belong to credit
qualifying, including high-yield sectors represented by SIMM buckets 7-12.
Credit non-qualifying is reserved for securitizations and other exposures
governed by the non-qualifying risk class.

oneOf.description: Credit-qualifying exposure assigned to an ISDA SIMM sector bucket.

sector.description: Sector bucket used for credit-qualifying delta aggregation.

oneOf.description: Credit non-qualifying exposure, typically a securitization.

SimmCreditSector.description:
SIMM credit sector for bucket assignment.

Maps reference entities to ISDA SIMM credit qualifying buckets.
See ISDA SIMM v2.6 Table 2.

oneOf.description: Bucket 1: IG sovereigns including central banks.
Bucket 2: IG financials including government-backed financials.
Bucket 3: IG basic materials, energy, and industrials.
Bucket 4: IG consumer goods and services.
Bucket 5: IG technology, telecommunications.
Bucket 6: IG health care, utilities, local government, and government-backed corporates.
Bucket 7: HY / non-rated sovereigns including central banks.
Bucket 8: HY / non-rated financials including government-backed financials.
Bucket 9: HY / non-rated basic materials, energy, and industrials.
Bucket 10: HY / non-rated consumer goods and services.
Bucket 11: HY / non-rated technology, telecommunications.
Bucket 12: HY / non-rated health care, utilities, local government, and government-backed corporates.
Residual bucket.

TrsDividendSettlement.description: Settlement timing for manufactured discrete dividends on an equity TRS.

oneOf.description:
Settle on the supplied dividend date, matching standard manufactured
dividend pass-through economics.
Defer the dividend to the reset period's contractual payment date.

end.description: End date for the TRS leg.

Pay total return, receive financing.

VmParameters.description:
Variation margin parameters.

These parameters govern the daily (or periodic) exchange of variation margin
under a CSA agreement. VM is exchanged to eliminate mark-to-market exposure.

# ISDA CSA Standard Terms

The 2016 VM CSA introduced standardized terms for variation margin:
- Zero threshold for in-scope entities
- Daily exchange with T+1 settlement
- Cash or highly liquid securities as collateral

# Example

```
use finstack_quant_margin::{MarginTenor, VmParameters};
use finstack_quant_core::currency::Currency;
use finstack_quant_core::money::Money;

let vm_params = VmParameters {
    threshold: Money::from((10_000_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    mta: Money::from((500_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    rounding: Money::from((10_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    independent_amount: Money::from((0_i64, Currency::USD)),
    frequency: MarginTenor::Daily,
    settlement_lag: 1,
};
```

frequency.description:
Margin call frequency.

Under BCBS-IOSCO, daily margin exchange is required.

independent_amount.description:
Independent Amount (IA) / Additional Margin.

Fixed collateral amount required regardless of exposure.
Often used for credit enhancement or as a buffer.

mta.description:
Minimum Transfer Amount (MTA).

Margin calls below MTA are not made. BCBS-IOSCO permits combined
IM+VM MTA up to €500,000 equivalent.

rounding.description:
Rounding increment for margin amounts.

Margin calls are typically rounded to the nearest multiple of this amount.

settlement_lag.description:
Settlement lag in business days (T+n).

Standard is T+1 for VM under 2016 VM CSA.

threshold.description:
Threshold amount below which no margin is exchanged.

Under BCBS-IOSCO rules for covered entities, VM threshold must be zero.
Legacy bilateral CSAs may have non-zero thresholds.
